result.title: Video-DCI: How Far Are VLM Agents from Human Viewers in Direct Video Corpus Interaction?
result.summary: Humans answer complex visual questions by inspecting short moments, updating what they know, and redirecting attention toward missing evidence. Existing video benchmarks, however, often provide the relevant video, evaluate only final answers or isolated localization, or permit textual shortcuts, leaving multi-round visual evidence seeking underexplored. We introduce Video-DCI, a diagnostic benchmark and functionally matched human-agent protocol for Direct Video-Corpus Interaction. It comprises DCI-Loc for temporal evidence localization and DCI-QA for end-to-end discovery, retention, and composition of cross-video evidence. In DCI-QA, videos within each pool are topically related, yet every answer requires hidden temporal evidence from multiple videos. Given only the question and video pool, humans and agents iteratively inspect bounded local windows, retain supporting evidence, and answer with cited temporal spans. Human trajectories provide reference curves for evidence acquisition and use across rounds. Experiments reveal a consistent retrieval-to-grounding gap. On DCI-Loc, frontier VLMs often retrieve and expose the reference moment, yet convert far less of this exposure into precise final citations than the human reference. On DCI-QA, the loss begins earlier and compounds across videos. Ablation studies further confirm that iterative search outperforms one-shot retrieval. Multi-round search is therefore necessary but insufficient: current agents accumulate candidates and observations more readily than precise, jointly sufficient evidence.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Video-DCI 诊断基准与人类对齐协议，用 DCI-Loc 和 DCI-QA 评估 VLM agent 在多轮视频证据定位、保留及跨视频组合上的表现，并报告「检索到落地」的差距。
AI.relevance_reason: 其多轮局部窗口检视、证据累积与带引用作答的评估，直接对应 LOOK/STOP 的收益成本与视觉证据筛选问题；可供核查「已暴露证据却未转为精确引用」是否源于状态保留或停止决策。
